standard.name: Full-support finite-simplex interior restriction, deliberately stronger than response-kernel positivity
Fixed interior positivity for a finite multinomial model

definitions.name: Three-item conditional missingness graph class
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak G_3=\left\{G=(I_X\cup I_R,E_G):E_G\subseteq\{X_j\to R_i:i,j\in I\}\cup\{R_j\to R_i:i\ne j\},\ G[I_R]\text{ is acyclic}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Uniform target-law identification
definitions.construction: \[\operatorname{UID}_X(G)=1\Longleftrightarrow\left[\forall p^{(0)},p^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_+(G),\ C_{\#}p^{(0)}=C_{\#}p^{(1)}\Rightarrow\sum_r p^{(0)}(x,r)=\sum_r p^{(1)}(x,r)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\right].\]

definitions.name: Complete3 certificate language
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal L_3\) has two terminal forms. An \(\mathrm{ID}\) term contains eight expressions formed from the coordinates of \(q\) by finite sums, products, and quotients; every quotient denominator is encoded as \(q(A)=\sum_{w\in A}q_w\) for a checker-certified nonempty event \(A\subseteq\mathcal W\). Its trace uses graph factorization, conditional independence, grouped fixing, intervention fixing, or Chen odds-ratio identities, and each constructor records all input and output divisors. A \(\mathrm{NONID}\) term contains two rational \(64\)-cell tables, their graph-factorized conditional tables, exact equality of their \(27\) coarsened cells, strict-positivity checks, and a named cell where their target marginals differ.

definitions.name: Exact certificate checker
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Check}_3(G,\gamma)\) parses \(\gamma\in\mathcal L_3\), evaluates every graph and rational identity by exact arithmetic, verifies for every graph-factorization, conditional-independence, grouped-fixing, intervention-fixing, and odds-ratio constructor that each input and output divisor is \(q(A)\) for an explicitly encoded nonempty event \(A\subseteq\mathcal W\), and verifies every \(\mathrm{NONID}\) table entry, factorization, coarsened-cell equality, strict-positivity inequality, and target-cell inequality.

definitions.name: Certified initial reduction
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Known}_3(G)\) applies, in order, the self-censoring twin compiler, the positive criss-cross twin compiler, the no-self-censoring/no-colluder full-law formula compiler, and the direct-association propensity compiler; it returns the first accepted \(\mathcal L_3\) certificate and otherwise returns \(\mathrm{unresolved}\).

definitions.name: Canonical list of the residual classes
definitions.construction: Encode \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\) by the \(15\)-bit word listing the nine possible \(X_j\to R_i\) arrows followed by the six possible \(R_j\to R_i\) arrows in lexicographic index order. For \(K\in\mathfrak R_{34}\), let \(\operatorname{can}(K)\) be its lexicographically least relabelling, and define \(\mathcal K_{34}=(G^{(1)},\ldots,G^{(34)})\) by sorting the \(34\) values \(\operatorname{can}(K)\) lexicographically.

definitions.name: Exceptional-stratum rational-inverse test
definitions.construction: For each \(G^{(k)}\in\mathcal K_{34}\), express the graph factorization and the \(27\) coarsening equations as a polynomial ideal over \(\mathbb Q\), localize at the product of the \(64\) full-cell coordinates and the \(27\) observed-cell coordinates, and split only on the vanishing or nonvanishing of rank minors and certificate denominators encountered in the residual derivation. On each resulting stratum \(\mathcal S\), exact Groebner elimination and multiplication-matrix minimal polynomials determine whether the residue class of \(p_X(x)\) lies in \(\mathbb Q(q_w:w\in\mathcal W)\), lies in a proper finite algebraic extension, or varies within the algebraic fibre. Positivity and actual nonidentification are certified separately by the analytic \(\mathcal L_3\) formula or rational twin in the same ledger row. This is a finite graph-specific function-field calculation, not generic real quantifier elimination.

definitions.name: Residual certificate-synthesis handle
definitions.construction: For each \(G^{(k)}\in\mathcal K_{34}\), begin with a pattern-indexed state carrying its observed kernel and selection provenance; close the state under licensed intervention-tree steps, grouped partial-order fixing, conditional-independence substitutions, and reference-cell odds-ratio factorization. Split on every rank minor and candidate divisor encountered, apply \(\operatorname{AlgTest}_3\) on each exceptional stratum, and use exact finite response-fibre calculations to derive either a rational observed-marginal formula or a rational positive twin family that is expressed and checked analytically in \(\mathcal L_3\).

definitions.name: Machine-checkable residual outcome ledger
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal D_{34}\) is an exactly \(34\)-row table indexed by \(\mathcal K_{34}\). Row \(k\) records the full \(15\)-bit edge word of \(G^{(k)}\), an exhaustive list of its positive rank and divisor strata, the value of \(\operatorname{AlgTest}_3\) for all eight target coordinates on each exceptional stratum, one analytic \(\mathcal L_3\) certificate covering every listed stratum, the exact \(\operatorname{Check}_3\) acceptance result, and the certificate operation count.

definitions.name: Complete3 construction handle
definitions.construction: Instantiate \(\operatorname{Complete}_3\) by running \(\operatorname{Known}_3\), applying simultaneous item relabelling and graph-inclusion transport to accepted certificates, and otherwise locating the unique canonical representative in \(\mathcal K_{34}\) and reading its accepted certificate from \(\mathcal D_{34}\); return the transported accepted \(\mathcal L_3\) certificate.

definitions.name: Compiled rational plug-in estimator
definitions.construction: \[\widehat p_X=F_G(\widehat q),\qquad \widehat q_w=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{W_j=w\},\] with a fixed unit pseudocount in all \(27\) cells only on samples where a required empirical divisor is zero.

definitions.name: Bonferroni simultaneous region
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(G)=\left\{v\in\Delta_7:|v_x-\widehat p_X(x)|\le z_{1-\alpha/16}\sqrt{\widehat V_G(x,x)/n}\text{ for all }x\in\mathcal B\right\}.\]

statements.statement: \[|\mathfrak G_3|=25\cdot2^9=12800,\qquad |\{G\in\mathfrak G_3:X_i\not\to R_i\text{ for every }i\in I\}/\mathfrak S_3|=280.\]
statements.justification: The exact finite domain prevents completeness from being replaced by an asymptotic or generic claim.
statements.gap: The cited graphical papers do not enumerate this labelled three-item domain or its simultaneous-relabeling quotient.
statements.consumer: The graph count fixes the audit universe for the public flexMissing classifier tests.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(H=G[I_R]\).  A directed graph on three labelled response vertices is determined by a subset of the six possible off-diagonal arrows.  Count acyclic choices by the number \(m\) of edges in the underlying undirected skeleton.  For \(m=0,1,2,3\), respectively, the numbers of labelled acyclic orientations are
\[
1,\qquad {3\choose1}2=6,\qquad {3\choose2}2^2=12,\qquad 2^3-2=6.
\]
For \(m=2\) the skeleton is a forest, so every orientation is acyclic; for \(m=3\) exactly the two directed three-cycles are excluded.  Hence there are
\[
1+6+12+6=25
\]
possible response DAGs.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}allowed\text{-}edges}\) permits each of the nine arrows \(X_j\to R_i\) independently, and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}graph\text{-}class}\) imposes no further condition on them.  Therefore
\[
|\mathfrak G_3|=25\,2^9=12800.
\]

Now forbid the three self-censoring arrows.  For each response DAG there are \(2^6\) choices of the six remaining substantive-to-response arrows, so the resulting set \(\mathcal A\) has cardinality \(25\,2^6=1600\).  For completeness, the orbit-count identity used below follows by double counting
\[
\mathcal T=\{(\sigma,A)\in\mathfrak S_3\times\mathcal A:\sigma A=A\}.
\]
Counting first by \(\sigma\) gives \(|\mathcal T|=\sum_\sigma|\operatorname{Fix}(\sigma)|\).  For an orbit \(\mathcal O\) and any representative \(A_0\in\mathcal O\), the number of elements carrying \(A_0\) to a fixed \(A\in\mathcal O\) equals \(|\operatorname{Stab}(A_0)|\), while \(|\mathcal O|\,|\operatorname{Stab}(A_0)|=6\) by the explicit partition of \(\mathfrak S_3\) into those fibres.  Thus every orbit contributes exactly six pairs to \(\mathcal T\), and
\[
|\mathcal A/\mathfrak S_3|=\frac16\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_3}|\operatorname{Fix}(\sigma)|.
\]
The identity fixes all \(1600\) elements.  Fix a transposition, say \((12)\).  On the six response arrows, the orbit \(\{R_1\to R_2,R_2\to R_1\}\) must be absent in an invariant DAG, while the other two arrow orbits may be chosen as neither, both arrows into \(R_3\), or both arrows out of \(R_3\).  Thus precisely three response DAGs are fixed.  The six non-self substantive arrows form three two-element orbits, giving \(2^3=8\) invariant masks.  Hence every transposition fixes \(3\cdot8=24\) elements of \(\mathcal A\).  Under a three-cycle, the six response arrows form the two directed three-cycle orbits; acyclicity forces both absent.  The six substantive arrows form two orbits, so a three-cycle fixes \(2^2=4\) elements.  The double-count identity now gives
\[
|\mathcal A/\mathfrak S_3|
=\frac{1600+3\cdot24+2\cdot4}{6}
=280.
\]
This proves both asserted counts.

statements.statement: For every \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\), \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G)\), and \(q=C_{\#}p\), one has \(q_w>0\) for every \(w\in\mathcal W\), and therefore \(q(A)=\sum_{w\in A}q_w>0\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\mathcal W\). For each graph-factorization, conditional-independence, grouped-fixing, intervention-fixing, and odds-ratio constructor of \(\mathcal L_3\), every checker-accepted input or output divisor has this form; consequently every divisor in every checker-accepted \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate is strictly positive throughout \(\mathcal M_+(G)\).
statements.justification: The deliberately stronger full-support model must license every displayed division rule-by-rule, not merely by an informal positivity appeal.
statements.gap: The missing-data papers cited for fixing and odds-ratio identities generally assume positive response kernels; they do not audit this stricter raw-observed-marginal divisor grammar under full joint support.
statements.consumer: The checker can certify before evaluation that every formula returned to flexMissing is defined at every law in the stated model.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\), \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G)\), and \(q=C_{\#}p\).  For any \(w\in\mathcal W\), define \(r(w)\in\mathcal B\) by \(r_i(w)=1\) when \(w_i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(r_i(w)=0\) when \(w_i=?\).  Choose \(x(w)\in\mathcal B\) with \(x_i(w)=w_i\) on observed coordinates and, for definiteness, \(x_i(w)=0\) on missing coordinates.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}coarsening\text{-}map}\) gives
\[
C(x(w),r(w))=w.
\]
Thus the fibre in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}law}\) is nonempty.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\) gives \(p(x(w),r(w))>0\), and hence
\[
q_w=\sum_{(x,r):C(x,r)=w}p(x,r)\ge p(x(w),r(w))>0.
\]
If \(\varnothing\ne A\subseteq\mathcal W\), choosing any \(w_0\in A\) yields
\[
q(A)=\sum_{w\in A}q_w\ge q_{w_0}>0.
\]

By Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}language}\), a quotient in an \(\mathrm{ID}\) term can be formed only with a denominator represented as \(q(A)\) for an explicitly encoded nonempty event \(A\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}checker}\) checks that condition for every input and output divisor of every graph-factorization, conditional-independence, grouped-fixing, intervention-fixing, and odds-ratio constructor.  The inequality just proved therefore applies to every divisor in every checker-accepted \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate, uniformly over \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G)\).

statements.statement: For every \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\), if \(\operatorname{Check}_3\) accepts an \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate with functional \(F_G\), then \(F_G(C_{\#}p)=p_X\) for every \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G)\). If it accepts a \(\mathrm{NONID}\) certificate \((p^{(0)},p^{(1)},x_0)\), then \(p^{(0)},p^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_+(G)\), \(C_{\#}p^{(0)}=C_{\#}p^{(1)}\), and \(p_X^{(0)}(x_0)\ne p_X^{(1)}(x_0)\).
statements.justification: A finite catalogue is meaningful only when every machine-readable branch independently certifies the graph-model claim.
statements.gap: GuoNabi2026InterventionTree proves soundness for intervention-tree traces, while pmlr-v115-bhattacharya20b proves grouped-fixing rules; neither checks a hybrid grammar with rational positive twins.
statements.consumer: flexMissing can reject a malformed formula or twin table before presenting it to an analyst.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\).  First suppose that \(\operatorname{Check}_3\) accepts an \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate \(\gamma\) with terminal expression \(F_G\).  We prove by induction along the finite trace of \(\gamma\) the invariant that every carried rational expression equals, for every \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G)\), the full-law quantity named by its trace label after substituting \(q=C_{\#}p\).

At an observed-coordinate leaf the invariant is exactly Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}law}\).  It is preserved by finite sums and products by ordinary algebra.  At a quotient node, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}denominator\text{-}safety}\) shows that the checker-certified denominator \(q(A)\) is nonzero, so division preserves the checked equality.  At a graph-factorization node, the checked identity is an instance of Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}graph\text{-}factorization}\).  At a conditional-independence node, substituting that factorization and summing the variables omitted by the node gives the checked conditional equality; all conditioning-event probabilities are nonzero by the denominator lemma.  At a grouped-fixing, intervention-fixing, or odds-ratio node, Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}checker}\) requires the checker to verify the corresponding rational identity from its already verified inputs and outputs.  Clearing its encoded denominators is legitimate by the denominator lemma, and the resulting exact identity therefore preserves the invariant.  These cases exhaust the grammar in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}language}\).

The eight terminal labels are the eight target marginals.  Hence, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), the terminal invariant and the definition of \(p_X\) give
\[
F_G(C_{\#}p)(x)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal B}p(x,r)=p_X(x).
\]

Now suppose that \(\operatorname{Check}_3\) accepts a \(\mathrm{NONID}\) certificate \((p^{(0)},p^{(1)},x_0)\).  By Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}language}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}checker}\), the parser checks normalization of each rational \(64\)-cell probability table, every entry is checked strictly positive, and the displayed conditional tables are checked against Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}graph\text{-}factorization}\) for \(G\).  Therefore \(p^{(0)},p^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_+(G)\).  For each \(w\in\mathcal W\), the checker also verifies the exact rational equality
\[
\sum_{(x,r):C(x,r)=w}p^{(0)}(x,r)
=
\sum_{(x,r):C(x,r)=w}p^{(1)}(x,r),
\]
which is \(C_{\#}p^{(0)}=C_{\#}p^{(1)}\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}law}\).  Finally, its named-cell check is precisely
\[
\sum_r p^{(0)}(x_0,r)\ne\sum_r p^{(1)}(x_0,r),
\]
or \(p_X^{(0)}(x_0)\ne p_X^{(1)}(x_0)\).  This proves both soundness assertions.

statements.statement: The deterministic procedure \(\operatorname{Known}_3\) returns accepted rational \(\mathrm{NONID}\) certificates for \(11200\) graphs containing a self-censoring arrow and for \(654\) additional no-self-censoring graphs containing a criss-cross obstruction; it returns accepted rational \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificates for \(496\) no-self-censoring/no-colluder graphs and for \(246\) additional direct-association graphs. Exactly \(204\) labelled graphs, forming \(34\) classes in \(\mathfrak R_{34}\), remain unresolved.
statements.justification: This theorem converts presolve calculations into a conservative, reproducible reduction without relying on the unaudited fixing-state search.
statements.gap: pmlr-v119-nabi20a classifies the full law and pmlr-v115-bhattacharya20b gives sufficient target-law rules, but neither supplies positive rational target-law certificates and an exact residual partition.
statements.consumer: The reduction limits manual residual analysis to \(34\) canonical cases and supplies regression tests for every already resolved graph.

statements.statement: For every \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G_{\mathrm{OR}})\), the Scenario 1 odds-ratio identification of Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020) specializes to \[p_X(x)=F_{\mathrm{OR}}(C_{\#}p)(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal B.\] Its encoding is accepted by \(\operatorname{Check}_3\), every divisor is positive by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}denominator\text{-}safety}\), and the intervention-tree workflow has no successful target-law trace on \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\), as documented by Guo and Nabi (2026).
statements.justification: This executable proposition is a regression fixture ensuring that the hybrid language retains the published odds-ratio success missed by the intervention tree.
statements.gap: The identifying content is already established by Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020), and the tree failure is already documented by Guo and Nabi (2026); only the exact checker encoding and divisor audit are project infrastructure, not novelty claims.
statements.consumer: flexMissing obtains a reproducible test that its hybrid evaluator accepts the published false-negative graph with a defined formula.
statements.proof_tex:
Write the three positive response kernels supplied by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}graph\text{-}factorization}\) on \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\) as
\[
\alpha_{z,s}(r_1)=p(r_1\mid X_3=z,R_2=s),\qquad
\beta_{u,t}(r_2)=p(r_2\mid X_1=u,R_3=t),\qquad
\gamma_u(r_3)=p(r_3\mid X_1=u),
\]
and put
\[
J_{st}(u)=\beta_{u,t}(s)\gamma_u(t)
=p(R_2=s,R_3=t\mid X_1=u).
\]
Every displayed factor is strictly positive because the full joint law is strictly positive.

For \(z,s\in\{0,1\}\), summing the factorization over the unshown substantive coordinates and over \(R_1\) where appropriate gives
\[
q(R_1=1,X_3^*=z,R_3=1,R_2=s)
=\alpha_{z,s}(1)\,q(X_3^*=z,R_3=1,R_2=s).
\]
The conditioning denominator is positive by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}denominator\text{-}safety}\), so
\[
a(z,s)=\alpha_{z,s}(1).
\]
Next define the positive quantity
\[
m_s(u)=\sum_{x_2,x_3}p_X(u,x_2,x_3)\alpha_{x_3,s}(1).
\]
Direct summation of the factorization gives, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
p(X_1=u,R_1=1,R_2=s,R_3=t)=m_s(u)J_{st}(u).
\]
Consequently
\[
c_s(u)=\frac{J_{s1}(u)}{J_{s0}(u)+J_{s1}(u)}.
\]

Let \(h(u)=\sum_{x_2}p_X(u,x_2,0)>0\).  The two observed reference-slice masses in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}odds\text{-}functional}\) are
\[
\begin{aligned}
q(X_1^*=u,X_3^*=0,R=(1,0,1))&=h(u)\alpha_{0,0}(1)J_{01}(u),\\
q(X_1^*=u,X_3^*=0,R=(1,1,1))&=h(u)\alpha_{0,1}(1)J_{11}(u).
\end{aligned}
\]
Using \(a(0,s)=\alpha_{0,s}(1)\), all positive factors cancel exactly and yield
\[
t(u)=\frac{J_{01}(u)}{J_{11}(u)}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{c_1(u)}+\frac{t(u)}{c_0(u)}
&=\frac{J_{10}(u)+J_{11}(u)}{J_{11}(u)}
 +\frac{J_{01}(u)}{J_{11}(u)}
   \frac{J_{00}(u)+J_{01}(u)}{J_{01}(u)}\\
&=\frac{\sum_{s,t\in\{0,1\}}J_{st}(u)}{J_{11}(u)}
=\frac{1}{J_{11}(u)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Finally, the complete-case cell satisfies
\[
q(X^*=x,R=\mathbf 1)
=p_X(x)\alpha_{x_3,1}(1)J_{11}(x_1)
=p_X(x)a(x_3,1)J_{11}(x_1).
\]
Substitution into Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}odds\text{-}functional}\) proves
\[
F_{\mathrm{OR}}(C_{\#}p)(x)=p_X(x)
\qquad(x\in\mathcal B).
\]
Each conditional probability just used is a ratio of two observed event marginals.  Expanding \(a\), \(c_s\), and \(t\) therefore expresses the calculation using only sums, products, and divisions by nonempty observed-event probabilities; all are positive by the denominator lemma.  The displayed factorization and cancellation form a finite odds-ratio trace, so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}checker}\) accepts its encoding.  The remaining algorithmic comparison is exactly the cited Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}guo\text{-}nabi\text{-}odds\text{-}tree\text{-}failure}\).

statements.statement: Using \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{res}}\), construct the ordered canonical list \(\mathcal K_{34}\) and fill every row of \(\mathcal D_{34}\). For each of its exactly \(34\) graph rows and every positive rank or divisor stratum, supply either an accepted \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate containing eight rational observed-law expressions with only universally positive observed-marginal divisors, or an accepted \(\mathrm{NONID}\) certificate containing two explicit strictly positive rational \(64\)-cell graph-Markov laws with equal \(27\)-cell coarsenings and different target mass at a named cell. Run \(\operatorname{AlgTest}_3\) on every exceptional stratum and establish that no uniformly identified row has output \(\mathrm{proper\ algebraic\ extension}\); certify exact row coverage, checker acceptance, and operation count in the ledger.
statements.justification: This is the genuine open content: exceptional positive fibres decide whether the requested rational certificate type is complete.
statements.gap: TikkaKarvanen2024 and LiMiaoShpitserTchetgenTchetgen2023 resolve restricted full-rank or complete models, while DuarteEtAl2023 supplies a generic polynomial oracle; none gives this graph-uniform rational interior dichotomy.
statements.consumer: The completed ledger turns every remaining flexMissing rejection into either a formula or a checkable positive countermodel and supplies the finite converse audit.

statements.statement: Using the accepted \(34\)-row ledger \(\mathcal D_{34}\) as a load-bearing converse certificate, there is an explicit instantiation of \(\operatorname{Complete}_3\) and a numerical integer \(B\) such that, for every \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\), the procedure terminates with \(\operatorname{cost}_3(\operatorname{Complete}_3(G))\le B\), its output is accepted by \(\operatorname{Check}_3\), and \[\operatorname{Complete}_3(G)\text{ has terminal type }\mathrm{ID}\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{UID}_X(G)=1.\] On the \(\mathrm{ID}\) branch it returns eight denominator-safe rational expressions \(F_G\); on the other branch it returns explicit strictly positive rational observational twins. The converse uses the ledger's exhaustive canonical coverage and exceptional-stratum \(\operatorname{AlgTest}_3\) outcomes, not generic real quantifier elimination. On the no-self-censoring/no-colluder subdomain the \(\mathrm{ID}\) output reduces to the target marginal of the full-law functional of Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020), while \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\) belongs to that subdomain and is not accepted by the intervention-tree workflow.
statements.justification: The equivalence, explicit certificates, and finite operation bound form the publishable theorem-level classification rather than a lookup table.
statements.gap: pmlr-v119-nabi20a proves an iff criterion only for the full law; pmlr-v115-bhattacharya20b and GuoNabi2026InterventionTree are sound but incomplete for the target law.
statements.consumer: The public flexMissing workflow receives a total graph decision with independently checkable evidence.

statements.statement: For every \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\), a successful \(\operatorname{Tree}_3(G)\) trace or \(\operatorname{GroupFix}_3(G)\) trace transports to an \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate returned by \(\operatorname{Complete}_3(G)\). Both acceptance-set inclusions are strict: \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\) is classified \(\mathrm{ID}\) through the published functional \(F_{\mathrm{OR}}\) and is not accepted by either fixing search. On every graph with no self-censoring arrow and no colluder, the returned target functional is algebraically equal to the target marginal of the full-law odds-ratio functional of Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020).
statements.justification: This statement makes the exact improvement over the closest constructive comparators auditable.
statements.gap: The two published fixing approaches cover complementary sufficient regimes and explicitly leave completeness open; the full-law theorem does not compare their target-law acceptance sets.
statements.consumer: Analysts can retain every currently supported flexMissing graph while gaining certified odds-ratio and residual branches.

statements.statement: Fix \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\) with an \(\mathrm{ID}\) output and \(\epsilon\in(0,1/64)\). Uniformly over \(p\in\mathcal M_{\epsilon}(G)\), \[\sqrt n\{\widehat p_X-p_X\}=\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\varphi_G(W_j;q)+o_p(1)\rightsquigarrow N_8(0,V_G(q)),\] where \(V_G(q)\) may be singular, \(\widehat V_G\to_p V_G(q)\), and \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{p\in\mathcal M_{\epsilon}(G)}\Pr_p\{p_X\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(G)\}\ge1-\alpha.\]
statements.justification: A classifier-returned formula becomes usable only with automatic joint uncertainty quantification that respects simplex singularity.
statements.gap: MalinskyShpitserTchetgenTchetgen2022 and Chen2022PatternGraphs derive model-specific influence functions; GuoNabi2026InterventionTree uses recursive parametric weighting rather than syntax-directed inference for arbitrary rational certificates.
statements.consumer: flexMissing can attach simultaneous uncertainty regions to every newly accepted three-item graph without assuming an invertible eight-dimensional covariance.

statements.statement: For the graph \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\), the Guo--Nabi intervention-tree procedure has no successful trace identifying the target law \(p_X\).

statements.statement:
For independent observations on a fixed finite sample space with probability vector \(q\), the empirical probability vector satisfies
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat q-q)\rightsquigarrow
N\!\left(0,\operatorname{diag}(q)-qq^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]

attestation.note: The finite-multinomial specialization is stated here; the stable DOI is supplied because no verbatim transcription is available in the frozen core.

sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling of the \(27\)-cell coarsened record \(W=C(X,R)\).
sampling_model.treatment: No treatment assignment is present; the causal object is the target law under the missingness DAG.
sampling_model.overlap: The identification model has full joint support, deliberately stronger than response-kernel positivity. For uniform inference only, \(p\in\mathcal M_{\epsilon}(G)\) for a fixed \(\epsilon>0\), which bounds every allowed observed-event divisor away from zero without strengthening the classification model.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No infinite-dimensional nuisance is estimated; \(F_G\), its derivative, and \(V_G\) are evaluated at the empirical multinomial vector with a fixed unit pseudocount only when required.

estimand_functional: \(p_X=F_G(q)\) on the \(\mathrm{ID}\) branch; the \(\mathrm{NONID}\) branch supplies \(C_{\#}p^{(0)}=C_{\#}p^{(1)}\) with \(p_X^{(0)}\ne p_X^{(1)}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give a sound-and-complete graphical criterion for full-law identification under no self-censoring and no colluders, Scenario 1 identifies the odds-rescue graph, and the Conclusion leaves complete target-law characterization open.
Proposition 1 gives sufficient grouped partial-order fixing conditions for target-law identification, and Section 6 leaves efficient search and completeness open.
Algorithm 1 and Theorem 1 give a constructive sound intervention-tree procedure, while Section 8 states that it is incomplete and misses an odds-ratio-identifiable graph.
Theorems 1--2 identify categorical-colluder full laws under identifiable colluder equations and full-rank conditions.
Theorem 1 reduces finite discrete causal bounds and point identification to polynomial optimization with sharpness at global completion.
The paper derives a semiparametric efficiency bound and augmented inverse-probability estimator for the no-self-censoring odds-ratio model.

tldr: On a deliberately stronger full-support finite model than the response-kernel positivity standard in the missing-data literature, a finite certificate calculus classifies uniform recovery of the eight-cell target law for all \(12800\) binary three-item conditional-MNAR DAGs. The novel kernel is the \(34\)-class residual dichotomy, its canonical machine-checkable ledger with an explicit exceptional-stratum rational-inverse audit, the sound-and-complete \(\operatorname{Complete}_3\) equivalence, and a strict acceptance frontier over both published fixing procedures. The odds-ratio graph already identified by Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser and reported as an intervention-tree false negative by Guo and Nabi is retained only as an executable regression exhibit. Every accepted formula has rule-by-rule positive observed-marginal divisors and compiles to joint multinomial inference on fixed interior subclasses.

project_justification.gap: Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser give a complete criterion for the full law but explicitly leave target-law completeness open. Grouped fixing and intervention trees provide complementary constructive sufficient procedures, and their known odds-ratio false negative does not supply the missing converse. Rank-based colluder results do not answer the graph-uniform question on positive rank-degenerate strata.
project_justification.niche: With exactly three binary items, the graph universe, coarsened law, and every certificate are finite, yet the target-law fibre remains richer than the full-law obstruction criterion. The unresolved \(34\) relabelling classes isolate the smallest setting where a complete target-law converse, rational-versus-algebraic inversion, and strict comparison of the two fixing acceptance sets can be audited exhaustively.
project_justification.fill: The project builds a typed hybrid certificate language with a rule-by-rule divisor theorem, constructs a canonical \(34\)-row outcome ledger carrying exact exceptional-stratum inverse tests, proves the ledger yields a total sound-and-complete classifier with a numerical operation bound, and compiles accepted rational formulas into joint multinomial inference.

related_work: Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020, Theorems 1--2, Scenario 1, and Conclusion) establish the full-law iff frontier, already identify the odds-rescue graph through Chen factorization, and explicitly separate that result from the still-open target-law completeness problem. Bhattacharya, Nabi, Shpitser, and Robins (2020, Proposition 1, Lemma 2, and Section 6) introduce grouped partial-order fixing and induced selection subproblems but leave completeness and general search open. Guo and Nabi (2026, Algorithm 1, Theorem 1, Figure E.2(a), and Section 8) turn intervention fixing into an executable tree and document the same odds-ratio graph as a false negative; that graph is a regression exhibit here, not a new identification result. Tikka and Karvanen (2024, Theorems 1--2 and Section 8) solve categorical colluder equations under full-rank conditions; their result informs the ledger's audit of every positive rank-degenerate stratum but is not treated as a graph-uniform comparator. Li, Miao, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023) regain full-law recovery in a self-censoring model under completeness, a restricted model outside the unrestricted graph-uniform target. Duarte et al. (2023, Theorem 1 and Sections 4--6) provide a polynomial-program audit oracle for finite models, whereas the ledger requires graph-specific rational-function-field tests and analytic certificates without generic real quantifier elimination. Malinsky, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2022), Chen (2022), and Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2022) inform the compiled inference layer; no efficiency comparison to their model-specific estimators is claimed. The present full-support condition is deliberately stronger than the response-kernel positivity used in the graphical missing-data literature.
technical_internal_limitation: A rational polynomial parameterization alone does not imply the rational certificate dichotomy: an injective map can have only a non-rational algebraic inverse, and an exact nonidentifying fibre can contain only irrational parameter points. The \(34\)-row ledger therefore applies \(\operatorname{AlgTest}_3\) on every exceptional positive stratum; finite enumeration, generic rank, and generic algebraic decidability cannot discharge Open-ended Question 1. The early kill test is residual case 6 with factorization \(p(r\mid x)=p(r_1\mid x_3)p(r_2\mid x_1,r_1)p(r_3\mid x_1,r_2)\): a uniformly identified target with unavoidable non-rational inverse, a required divisor outside the observed-marginal grammar, or a nonidentified fibre admitting no rational positive twins would obstruct Theorem 3.
honest_scope: The exact graph count, large certificate reduction, self-censoring twins, and criss-cross twins have presolve evidence but remain \(\mathrm{to\text{-}prove}\) in this core. The odds-rescue identification is published and appears only as an executable regression proposition. The \(34\)-class residual dichotomy, canonical outcome ledger, exceptional-stratum rational-generation audit, explicit numeric operation bound, strict two-method acceptance frontier, and compiled simultaneous coverage are open. The classification model imposes full joint support, a deliberately stronger finite-simplex interior restriction than standard response-kernel positivity, but no stronger classification assumption; the fixed \(\epsilon\)-interior subclass is used only for uniform inference. The proposal assumes the missingness graph is supplied, fixes binary cardinality at three, excludes latent variables and response-to-substantive arrows, and does not address graph learning, boundary laws, continuous variables, or unpublished results that may follow the March 2026 talk.
